Consult Summary:
- 32-year-old male with 1.5–2 months of recurrent, transient right-hand paresthesia with episodic limb weakness and gait change; urgent TIA clinic referral arranged with ED precautions provided.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Intermittent “weird symptoms” over ~1.5–2 months.
- Symptom details:
  - Right-hand pins and needles; perceived right arm weakness.
  - Right leg feels weaker during episodes; colleague noted abnormal gait.
  - Difficulty holding a cup and drinking during episodes (past few days).
  - Sensation of “something in the throat” during episodes; no persistent swallowing difficulty.
  - General fatigue and weakness; intermittent nausea; decreased motivation.
  - No speech difficulty; no visual changes reported (wears glasses at baseline).
- Timeline:
  - Initial fatigue episodes lasted a couple of days, then returned to baseline.
  - Neurologic episodes began ~1.5–2 months ago.
  - Frequency increased from initially “once a week” or “once a month” (conflict noted) to a couple of times per day.
  - No current symptoms at time of consult.
- Triggers/relievers: Not reported.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No ongoing dysphagia outside episodes.
  - No dysarthria or visual symptoms during episodes.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic illnesses reported.
- No prior TIA or stroke.
- Post–family event screening reportedly normal: blood pressure, cholesterol, and diabetes checks (dates/values not provided).
- Asthma: not confirmed (raised by clinician; patient did not confirm).

Medications:
- Aspirin 75 mg once daily (self-initiated; taken to reduce stroke/MI risk).
- Allergies: Penicillin.

Social History:
- Occupation: Medical doctor (plastic surgery).
- Lives with wife.
- Tobacco: Never smoker.
- Alcohol and other substances: Not documented.

Family History:
- Father had carotid artery surgery to reduce stroke risk.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed/documented (telehealth; video lost during visit).
- Vitals: Not documented.

Investigations:
- Prior (patient-reported): Blood pressure, cholesterol, and diabetes testing normal (no dates/values).
- Planned via TIA clinic: Carotid ultrasound; possible brain imaging (details pending).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Recurrent transient focal neurologic symptoms (right-hand paresthesia; transient right arm/leg weakness; gait change; intermittent throat sensation) — concerning for TIA.
  - Urgent referral to TIA clinic placed; expected contact and appointment within 1–2 days.
  - Patient advised to call TIA clinic/PALS today or tomorrow to confirm scheduling; numbers to be provided in chart.
  - Emergency precautions: If symptoms recur and are prolonged/persistent, attend the Emergency Department immediately.
  - Safety net: Contact GP service if delays in scheduling or for further guidance.
  - Anticipated tests at clinic: Carotid ultrasound; possible brain imaging.
- Issue 2: Self-initiated daily aspirin use.
  - Aspirin 75 mg once daily taken without prior medical recommendation.
  - Risks/benefits and indication not discussed in detail today; no changes to medication documented.
- Issue 3: Fatigue, intermittent nausea, decreased motivation.
  - Not specifically evaluated or managed during this visit; relationship to neurologic episodes unclear.

General Plan items:
- None beyond above.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Exact DOB; full medication reconciliation (including OTC/supplements); alcohol/substance use; vitals; focused neurologic exam; precise episode durations and onset times; cardiovascular risk assessment; driving/operating machinery advice; counseling regarding aspirin use; comprehensive ROS.
- Internal conflicts: Initial episode frequency described as “once a week” vs “once a month.” Onset described as “past month or so” vs “1.5–2 months.”
- Transcript quality: Remote consult with intermittent connection issues and loss of video; some unclear/inaudible segments.
